articles.title: How to choose an elevator service company
articles.description: A short, plain-English guide for building owners and property managers.
articles.author: Summit Vertical Services
articles.lede: A few things separate a company that keeps you informed from one that does not.

summary.label: The short version
summary.intro: If you are deciding who maintains your elevators, here is what to look for.
points: They cover your equipment across manufacturers, not just one brand.
They keep the maintenance log, test records, and written program together per unit.
You can see status and history without chasing anyone.

articles.body:
Choosing who maintains your elevators comes down to a few plain things.

First, do they cover your equipment across manufacturers, or only one brand? A building with mixed makes is easier to service when one team handles all of it and sources parts across manufacturers.

Second, ask how they keep records. A maintenance log, test records, and the written program should live together per unit, and you should be able to see them without chasing anyone.

Third, ask what happens when something is down after hours. A real on-call path matters more than a line on a website.

faqs.q: How often should elevators be maintained?
faqs.a: Most passenger elevators are on a monthly or quarterly maintenance plan. What applies to your building depends on the equipment and what your jurisdiction has adopted; your authority having jurisdiction and your service company confirm the schedule.

articles.title: Reading your service history
articles.description: What the log tells you, and how to spot a unit that needs attention.
articles.author: Summit Vertical Services
articles.body:
A service history is more useful than a single visit. Look for repeat callbacks on the same unit, parts replaced more than once, and gaps where a scheduled visit was missed.
